name: Azure Serathiel
age: No explicit age stated. The card frames him as having 'transcended mortal ken' rather than giving a number — ageless/timeless. Stage XI Dissonance at Level 307, reached by walking toward something that could end him and remaining coherent, implies a lifetime (or more) of sustained discipline. Reads as a composed, seasoned adult — never youthful, never frail-old.
body: No height or build given directly. The statline is Dexterity-first (728 SS, the highest Dexterity in the migration) with Vitality (382 A) and Resilience (440 S) well below it and Dominion at 286 B, his own floor — a finesse blade-saint's frame built for evasion and precision, not mass or ground-holding. Wind-Wreathed Grace has him moving like drifting mist, footfalls that disturb no grass — lean and economical, not a powerhouse.
texture: a faint aeolian breath (wind, still air) rather than vocal fry or growl
spare and unhurried — no wasted syllables
energy: banked stillness by design — a regulated setpoint, not a mood; Ardency (fire, passion, aggression) sits deliberately mid on his sheet, so the default reads serene and contained rather than flat or dead. The one described failure mode is a regulator held against a load it cannot overcome: no rise under provocation, then a delayed, total discharge once the load lifts.
register: aphoristic and ceremonial — address rather than conversation. Short, often paradox-structured declaratives (see the epigraph), a master's economy of words rather than a talker's.

reference_direction: Male, medium-low pitch, smooth and unforced with almost no rasp. Delivery is hushed and economical — he under-speaks rather than projects, each line placed the way his footfalls land: present, but disturbing nothing. Pace is unhurried but not slow; short, often paradox-shaped sentences delivered with total composure, vowels held rather than clipped. No regional real-world accent — a placeless, formal, faintly ceremonial cadence, like a vow spoken rather than a conversation held. Comparable to a serene martial-arts master or monastery-trained mentor's voice: still water with a blade under it, not a warrior's bark — and one that, on the rare occasion the regulation fails, can drop that stillness all at once rather than raising by degrees.
one_line: A hushed, unhurried sword-saint's voice — serenity worn as discipline rather than temperament, with a coiled stillness that breaks all at once, not by degrees, if the pressure ever exceeds what it can hold.
